title: BLITZ trader's checklist size (no fit) - thin lead, not adopted
question: Does a trader's written-down checklist (no fitting at all) size BLITZ better than a fitted score?
verdict: BLITZ trader's checklist (no fit: strong break, day already moving, not the first signal, room to the next pool, with the 15m structure; 0-1 boxes x0.5, 2-3 x1, 4-5 x1.5): H1 R/risk +0.195 (today +0.165, multiplier-shuffle p 0.033), 25K 2-week pass/fail 42.9/36.1 (today 36.1/37.8), slot $287/mo (today $270); H2 R/risk +0.222 (today +0.200, multiplier-shuffle p 0.097), 25K 2-week pass/fail 33.3/34.8 (today 36.2/34.8), slot $50/mo (today $37); 2021-25 R/risk +0.019 (today +0.013, multiplier-shuffle p 0.123), 25K 2-week pass/fail 23.6/48.3 (today 20.4/50.2), slot $-38/mo (today $-40). Better per unit of risk in every span and 6 of 7 years, but the out-of-sample shuffles reach it 10-12% of the time, the H2 2-week pass drops, and it was written after the fact table was seen (two boxes are the known later-break / trend-day facts). Thin lead, not adopted.
